results.q: Is Circles a social welfare Project?
results.a:
Yes, Circles provide Universal Basic Income (UBI) to all people in the form of Circles Points.




Everyday, the Circles app will generate 24 points to each users, inclusive to everyone, regardless of their socioeconomic or geographical background.




The Circles Points are provided with the intention to serve as additional resources to support the fulfillment of daily needs through the exchange of goods/services based on mutual agreement.




Circles aim to provide a complementary cashless solution to all people everywhere to realise joyful, fulfilled, & meaningful lives in which daily needs are met as communities help each other to grow.

Yes, Circles can create new opportunities, especially between vendors.




For example: you can build partnerships with other vendors who provide raw materials needed for the goods/services of your business. This way, you can use Circles Points or a combination of Circles Points and cash for your supply or raw materials.

results.q: Is Circles useful for vulnerable groups (the poor, disabled, elderly etc.?)
results.a:
Circles offers benefit to all people without exception. 




The main goal of Circles is to provide complementary means to support the fulfillment of daily needs through the exchange of goods or services with Circles Points.




The Circles app can be used by everyone at anytime and anywhere, as long as they have smartphone and access to internet. In other word, Circles is given to us simply because we exist.

results.q: Can Circles demonstrate cooperation and trust between people?
results.a:
Circles can be evidence of a trust-based relationship in society.




In order to send or receive Circles Points, both users need to establish trust relation between each other within the app. Only then users are be able to use Circles Points to exchange for goods/services with each other.




If the trust relation is not achieved, the system will not work, and the transaction cannot be carried out.

results.q: Does Circles represent traditional Balinese & Indonesian value?
results.a:
Yes. Circles reflects the principles of mutual cooperation & care "asah, asih, asuh" embodied within the Indonesian traditional value.




Furthermore, Circles is a form of implementation of Tat Twam Asi (I am you, you are me), which is one of the core philosophies of the Balinese community, where we help each other and treat others as we treat ourselves.




Circles' mission is to support the fulfillment of daily needs of everyone based on mutual trust and agreement, not only for themselves but also for others in the local community.

results.q: Does Circles offer a solution for making UBI Initiatives more viable?
results.a:
Yes. Circles is a model that can be an extension of the UBI (universal basic income) program with great potential for an inclusive and feasible implementation.




This type of UBI does not require large cash payments, which are usually borne by the government or individuals, and does not cause/affect overall inflation.




In the world of Circles, everyone can benefit without exception.
